subject: Can a function be added as a geom?

messages.author: e6485f8b06f8dbfc
messages.subject: Can a function be added as a geom?
parts:
Hi. As I was looking at Ian's video on extending Plot Builder, I thought about adding a geom for Pareto Plots, which would remove an obstacle for some people looking at Deducer as a possibility.

The problem is that I don't know about the innards of geoms, so I thought that maybe I could build a function that returns a properly adjusted geom_bar and make it pass as a geom itself. The function is on the attached file, and it works fine for statements such as:

ggplot() + geom_myPareto(x=X,y=Y,data=DataPareto,colour = '#000000',fill = '#66ff33')

but of course it is not a true geom - and cannot get data.frame or aes, or any other parameters from ggplot().

The question is, can something like this be modified or wrapped so it can be added to Plot Builder as a geom? Or a template?

Suggestions would be much appreciated! Thanks,

Ben

messages.author: 1e82ea932416652e
messages.subject: Re: Can a function be added as a geom?
parts:
Ben,

A Pareto plot, with a “count” bar chart and a “percent total” line graph overlaid on the same plot, is not a single geom, but is a geom_bar() with a geom_line() (and probably a geom_point() overlaid on the geom_line()).

The last time I checked, ggplot2 didn't support multiple y axes on the same plot, so you can’t do such a graph in a single plot area. The closest you could come would be to arrange the two plots using grid.draw() {grid} or by using the viewport functions in {grid} to have the two plots arranged vertically (or side-by-side, if you prefer).

The basic code would look something like:

library(ggplot2)
library(grid)
p1 <- ggplot() + geom_bar()
p2 <- ggplot() + geom_line() + geom_point()
grid.draw(rbind(ggplotGrob(p1), ggplotGrob(p2), size = “first”)

You could also get a little fancier with {gtable}, per this Stack Overflow answer: http://stackoverflow.com/a/28256627/393354

I’m not familiar enough with Deducer’s plugin architecture to know if it could handle something like this.

Regards,

Tom
